title: Strings
summary: Join text, drop values into it, and ask a string about itself.

steps.title: Joining text
body: `+` between strings glues them together. This is called **concatenation**.
Nothing adds spaces for you. `first + last` would print `AdaLovelace`.
If one side is a string, the other side is turned into text too:

steps.explain: `+` works left to right. Once a string is involved it joins text. In the last line `1 + 2` is still two numbers, so it becomes `3` before meeting the string.

steps.title: String interpolation
body: Lots of `+` signs get hard to read. Put a `$` before the opening quote and you can drop values straight into the text inside `{ }`.
Anything inside the braces is real code: a variable, a calculation, a method call.
A colon adds formatting. `{price:F2}` shows exactly two decimal places:

steps.prompt: Complete the line so it prints `Hello, Sam! You have 3 messages.`
steps.explain: Without the `$` the braces would be printed literally. Without the braces you would get the word `user`.

options: Nothing: it is a compile error
steps.explain: There is no `$` before the string, so it is ordinary text and the braces mean nothing special. A very common slip.

steps.title: Asking a string about itself
body: A string comes with **members** you reach using a dot.
`word[0]` is the first character. Counting starts at **zero**, so the last character of `"Hello"` is `word[4]`.
> **Tip:** Strings never change. `word.ToUpper()` hands you a *new* string and leaves `word` as it was. To keep the result, store it: `word = word.ToUpper();`

steps.prompt: `string s = "Code";` Match each expression to its value.

steps.explain: `ToUpper()` returned `"DOJO"`, but nothing stored it. The original string is untouched.

steps.title: Fix the receipt
prompt: It compiles, but the output is wrong in three places. Fix it.
hints: Line 6: `3.5` needs to show as `3.50`. A format after a colon does that.
Line 7: the item name should be in capitals. You can call a method inside the braces.

steps.title: Cleaning and cutting text
body: Text that people type is messy. These members return a **new**, tidier string:
raw.Trim().ToLower()       // "fix login!"  (calls chain left to right)
"Ada Lovelace".LastIndexOf(' ')   // 3   (position of the last space; -1 if none)
`Substring(start, length)` crashes if it would run past the end, which is what `Math.Min` protects against:

steps.title: Initials for your badge
prompt: **Sidekick piece:** `sk` shows a badge with your initials next to the greeting: `[AL] Good morning, Ada Lovelace.`
Your code becomes the body of `static string Initials(string fullName)`. `fullName` is given; put the upper-case
first letter of the first word and of the **last** word in `result`.
Names always have at least two words here. Trim first, so stray spaces do not count as words.
starter: // fullName is given. Put the initials in result.
template: Dojo.Eq("three names use the first and the last", "GH", Initials("grace brewster hopper"));
Dojo.Eq("stray spaces are ignored", "LT", Initials("  linus torvalds "));
hints: The first letter is `clean.Substring(0, 1)`. The last word starts right after the last space: `clean.Substring(lastSpace + 1, 1)`.
Join them and call `.ToUpper()` on the result.

build.title: Your initials badge
build.unlocks: Your greeting now carries your initials badge.
transform: // Your initials badge: your own passing code from the code-dojo C# track (First steps > Strings).

steps.title: A branch name from a task title
prompt: **Sidekick piece:** after `sk add "Fix login redirect"`, Sidekick suggests `git switch -c sk/1-fix-login-redirect`.
The tail is a **slug**. Your code becomes the body of `static string Slug(string title)`. `title` is given; put the
slug in `result`, built in this order:
1. trim it and make it lower case;
3. turn every space and every `/` into `-`;
4. turn `--` into `-`, twice (so up to four dashes in a row shrink to one);
5. keep at most 40 characters, then trim `-` off both ends.
starter: // title is given. Put the slug in result.
template: Dojo.Eq("punctuation is removed", "ship-v20-ready", Slug("  Ship v2.0: ready!  "));
Dojo.Eq("slashes become dashes, runs of dashes shrink", "fix-login-logout", Slug("Fix: login / logout"));
Dojo.Eq("quotes and commas go", "dont-break-ana-s-build", Slug("Don't break Ana s build"));
Dojo.Eq("long titles stop at 40 characters", "refactor-the-payment-service-to-use-the", Slug("Refactor the payment service to use the new gateway"));
Dojo.Eq("no trailing dash after cutting", "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa", Slug(new string('a', 39) + " bbbb"));
hints: Chain the calls: `clean = clean.Replace(".", "").Replace("!", "")...;` Each `Replace` returns a new string.
To remove a `"` write `Replace("\"", "")`: `\"` is a quote inside a string.

build.title: Branch-name slug
build.unlocks: `sk add` now suggests a git branch name for every task.
transform: // Branch-name slug: your own passing code from the code-dojo C# track (First steps > Strings).
